title: Primary and standby processes
caption: WAL written on the primary flows through the walsender and walreceiver to the startup process, which replays it so read-only queries on the standby can see the data.

badges.meaning: A backend writes the commit's WAL record to pg_wal on the primary
The walsender reads the new WAL from pg_wal
The walsender streams WAL over TCP to the standby walreceiver
The walreceiver writes and fsyncs the WAL into the standby's own pg_wal
The startup process reads that WAL
The startup process replays (redoes) it into data files and KnownAssignedXids
A read-only query takes its snapshot from the replayed state

title: One commit reaches the replica
caption: Follow one COMMIT down the page: it is flushed, shipped, saved, replayed, becomes visible to a standby reader, and the standby reports its positions back.

badges.meaning: COMMIT flushes its WAL record on the primary
The walsender wakes and reads the new WAL (XLogSendPhysical)
The walreceiver gets the WAL, writes it and fsyncs it (XLogWalRcvFlush)
The startup process is woken and redoes the record (heap_redo)
A read-only SELECT on the standby now sees the row
The walreceiver sends a reply with write, flush and apply LSNs (XLogWalRcvSendReply)
The walsender gets the reply, which shows up in pg_stat_replication

title: Standby files and wire messages
caption: A standby is just a data directory with a few marker files plus WAL segments, and it talks to the primary with two small binary messages, 'w' going down and 'r' coming back.

badges.meaning: standby.signal: empty file that keeps the server in recovery
backup_label: from the base backup, says where replay starts
postgresql.auto.conf: holds primary_conninfo, the primary's address
pg_wal: WAL segments and timeline history written by the walreceiver and at promotion
'w' message: dataStart, walEnd, sendTime, then the WAL bytes
'r' message: writePtr, flushPtr, applyPtr, sendTime, replyRequested
